messages:
alex_m: Heads up — I’m seeing ~30 pods in Pending in cluster-usw2-gpu (mostly /batch and /training). CA didn't spin up new nodes. Quick logs show a bunch of Fit failures around packing even though total free GPUs exist.
maria_dev: Ugh. Can you paste a couple of FitPredicate failures? That usually points to fragmentation (lots of 1-GPU and a few 4-GPU jobs leaving unusable leftovers).
alex_m: here’s the scheduler event from one pod:
```
0/30 nodes are available: 30 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 15 node(s) didn't match node selector, 5 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate.
```
Also CA metrics say scale up skipped because no nodegroup would reduce unschedulable pods (expander=priority unset).
chen_infra: quick theory: we have pods that request `requests.gpu=1` but some have `limits.gpu=4` (copy/paste error). Scheduler treats the request; CA sim tries different instance types but our nodegroups are only 1xA100 and 8xA100 which leads to binpacking holes.
sanjay: I saw that too — some jobs were submitting with `resources.requests.nvidia.com/gpu: "1"` and `resources.limits.nvidia.com/gpu: "2"`. If requests != limits CA/KScheduler decisions get weird and it inflates CPU/memory packing estimates.
maria_dev: actionables: 1) audit recent batch job specs to normalize GPU request==limit; 2) add a small-GPU nodepool (1x A100-MIG slices or 1x T4) for lots of 1-GPU jobs; 3) tune CA expander to `least-waste` or consider Karpenter for mixed instance fits.
alex_m: for the audit you can run this to find mismatches quickly:
```
kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.namespace}/{.metadata.name} {.spec.containers[*].resources}{"\n"}{end}' | grep -E "gpu"
```
maria_dev: FYI MIG would help us slice A100 into many 1/2/4g partitions (if using A100s) — that reduces fragmentation massively. note: MIG is only on A100/H100 families.
chen_infra: plan I'm going to try tonight: create two new nodegroups in us-west-2: `gpu-small-mig` (A100 w/ MIG profiles, CA min=2,max=12) and `gpu-large` (4xA100 nodes, min=0,max=6). also enable cluster-autoscaler flag `--expander=least-waste` and `--balance-similar-node-groups` off for mixed sizes.
sanjay: will add a quick mutating webhook to validate GPU requests (reject mismatched request/limit) so we don’t keep introducing bad specs. simple failure for now is fine.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-042 (Pending GPU pods due to node packing fragmentation). Pager scheduled for infra oncall.
alex_m: timeline — try the nodegroups + CA flag change at 22:00 UTC, run audit script before and after. If we still see >10 Pending pods after 30m, rollback CA flags and open a deeper debug session.
maria_dev: also add a temporary affinity rule to prefer `gpu-small-mig` for pods labeled `job-size=small` so they don't land in huge nodes during the transition.
chen_infra: noted. I’ll post PRs for nodepool terraform and the webhook. tagging @sanjay for the webhook review.
sanjay: ack. I’ll review in the next hour. :thumbsup:
alex_m: thanks — appreciate the quick triage. keep updates here and I’ll notify owners of the affected training jobs to pause new submissions for 1h.
